opportunities.title: Entra ID Just Got a Perfect 10 — And Attackers Already Have It
opportunities.why_now: A CVSS 10.0 RCE flaw in Microsoft's core identity platform is being actively exploited in the wild right now, making it the most urgent patch item of the week.
opportunities.angle: Breaking-news patch alert: explain blast radius (anyone federating identity through Entra), confirm exploitation status, give a hard patch-by date

opportunities.title: 245 Million Downloads Later: North Korea's Rust Crate Backdoor Was Already Inside Your Build
opportunities.why_now: A nation-state actor slipped build-time malware into wildly popular Rust crates, turning routine `cargo build` into a supply-chain compromise vector.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive explainer: how the poisoned crates worked, who's exposed, and a checklist for auditing dependency trees this week

opportunities.title: GitLab's Zero-Click Flaw Went From Disclosure to Active Exploitation in Days — Here's the Patch Window You Missed
opportunities.why_now: CVE-2026-19478 is a zero-click GitLab bug already being exploited barely days after disclosure, collapsing the usual patch-cadence grace period.
opportunities.angle: Patch-cadence postmortem: timeline graphic from disclosure to exploit, plus why zero-click bugs in dev tooling deserve emergency-patch SLAs

opportunities.title: Russia's Phishing Crews Have a New Trick: Weaponizing Your Own OAuth Consent Screen
opportunities.why_now: Two independent reports this week confirm Russian-linked actors are abusing Google OAuth and WhatsApp device-linking flows to hijack accounts without stealing a single password.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor explainer: walk through the OAuth-abuse chain step by step and give defenders concrete consent-screen hardening tips
